session_title: Technology + Communication: Doing Something for Campus Stray Animals
theme: 宠物-云吸宠与校园公益

content.text: Hey, do you remember three months ago when we were talking about the campus 'Cat Seniors' guide, and I mentioned that the school's animal protection club wanted to spay/neuter stray animals and find them homes but lacked enough publicity? Well, I've actually joined the club now, and they urgently need a mini-program or H5 page to showcase information about animals available for adoption and spread the word on campus. Here's their poster. Do you think this kind of request is a piece of cake for you? We could collaborate—you handle the tech, and I'll take care of the content and promotion, helping 'Cat Seniors' and 'Dog Juniors' find homes? Just like how we moved from health projects to game collaborations before, turning our interests into real projects.

Haha, Xingwan, you social butterfly are exploring new territories again! Let me think—hmm, using a lightweight framework like Vue with cloud development, we can quickly set up an information display and application form page. It wouldn’t require too much work, and it has social value, which aligns with my philosophy of open-source sharing. This reminds me of the idea we discussed earlier about a campus cat catalog mini-program—now is the perfect time to put it into practice. It’s been almost three months since you gave me the "Cat Senior" healing package last time. Back then, I said I’d build a prototype, and now we can actually make it happen.

Great! I knew you'd be interested. Remember our previous health dashboard project? That time, we started with your health crisis—I tackled the issue of restructuring the proposal forms, and you developed the data dashboard. We established a social contract. This time, we can also discuss requirements, schedule, and launch plans as if starting a startup project. I’ll be responsible for organizing and beautifying each animal’s "resume," such as their personality, story, and health condition, using positive and truthful descriptions while avoiding pity-driven narratives—just as we discussed before, not romanticizing their stray situation but describing it in a friendly way.

Yes, just like what you mentioned earlier—'spayed/neutered, fully vaccinated, gentle and enjoys head pats.' I could also add a small feature like a 'virtual cloud feeding' check-in to increase engagement, similar to the point incentives on a health dashboard, encouraging user interaction. Remember when we collaborated on the game, and you treated failure emotions as a health metric? This time, the cloud feeding points can continue that fun, data-driven approach.

Look at this, I found some interface references for pet adoption apps. The design is simple and warm, highlighting a caring atmosphere. We can draw inspiration from this style to make the applet more appealing. I plan to promote it on the campus public account and confession wall, using my social media skills to handle the dissemination part. This reminds me of the project table image I shared in session 1, which presented ideas in a clear, structured way—I’ll use a similar approach to plan the promotion strategy this time.

Efficiency first! I've assessed it: the basic features can be completed within a week, and with the cloud feeding functionality added, it'll take about 10 days in total. We can open-source it on GitHub so other schools can reuse it, continuing the core value of technology changing the world. Xing Wan, how long will it take you to organize your resume? I remember during our health project, you worked quickly and put together a detailed proposal table in just a few days.

I'm quite curious and have already requested detailed information from the club. I expect to complete the first draft in about 3-4 days. By the way, we can draw on our previous experience with game collaborations to make the animal stories more vivid, such as "abandoned after the original owner graduated and left school, longing for a stable family," to strengthen the emotional bond. Just as we analyzed non-verbal collaboration in games, this time we can use stories to build an emotional connection between people and animals.

Great idea! We can start by creating an MVP (Minimum Viable Product), launch it quickly to gather feedback, and then iterate and optimize. Xing Wan, do you have a specific timeline for the promotion plan you're responsible for? Like when we collaborated on the game project and you marked 'Topic Collaboration: Games as Field Research' on the calendar, could you also create a detailed schedule for this one?

Yes, take a look at this—I've organized an online consultation session, similar to a video conference format, to help potential adopters learn about the animals. For promotion, within a week after the mini-program goes live, we plan to launch an intensive campaign on campus media, combined with club activities, to maximize exposure. This reminds me of the health data dashboard screenshot you shared earlier, where we used visualization to present issues—I'll also use clear charts to plan this promotion strategy.

Tech enthusiast mode activated! I'll start building the framework tonight and show you the prototype tomorrow. By the way, remember the social contract from our health project? That time we set up health points to redeem hotpot or milk tea for achieving goals. This time, we can also set team milestones, like completing development, launching promotions, and maintaining motivation. From the red terminal alerts in session 1 to this public welfare project now, our collaboration is becoming more and more continuous.

Haha, the mild 'workaholic' is back online! But I like this kind of efficiency. I'll balance my studies and this project well, just like the emphasis on diverse experiences in our past conversations. Lu Chenguang, you should also take care of your health—don’t pull all-nighters coding again. We can use the health dashboard to keep an eye on things, remember? In session 1, I said, "Don’t trade your health for code." This project is meaningful, but health is more important.

Don't worry, peer pressure can be turned into motivation! This project has social value, so I'm full of energy. Xingwan, when you organize the resumes, you can categorize them into several groups, such as cats, dogs, and other pets, to make it easier for front-end display. I'll consider responsive design during development to ensure compatibility with both mobile phones and computers. This reminds me of the health dashboard project where you asked me to design a visually appealing front-end interface—your aesthetic sense is on point. Could you help oversee the design this time too?

Alright, I'll categorize them by personality and story, giving each animal a unique 'character profile.' For promotion, I plan to use the name of an animal protection society to enhance credibility. Lu Chenguang, how should we design the cloud feeding feature? After a virtual check-in, can users earn points or badges? Just like in our game collaboration, where you suggested integrating the number of game failures into the health dashboard, should we also quantify fun interactions this time?

Yes, you can set up daily check-in reward points, and accumulate a certain number of points to unlock badges, such as 'Heart Feeder.' This can increase user engagement and aligns with the fun of lifelong learning. Technically, I use cloud development to store user data, ensuring it's lightweight and efficient. Remember in session 4, during the game process, we discussed the 'sense of presence' in instant sharing? The cloud feeding feature can also create a similar sense of remote participation.

Perfect! This is just like the real-time interaction in our game collaboration, enhancing the sense of involvement. I have a mild case of FOMO—fear of missing out on good ideas—so I’ll keep collecting feedback to optimize the content. Lu Chenguang, let’s schedule a time early next week to review the progress, just like we did in previous projects. Remember in session 2 when we said, "Sync progress weekly, like a small team"? Let’s maintain that collaborative rhythm this time too.

No problem, how about next Tuesday evening? I can present the preliminary interface and features. Xingwan, this collaboration is truly fantastic—turning our love for animals into meaningful public welfare practices, combined with technology dissemination, continues the continuity from health crises to gaming partners. From the brink of collapse in session 1 to now doing something for stray animals, the scope of our collaboration is expanding more and more.

Yes, from the 'Cat Senior' illustrated guide to actual projects, we're becoming more like research partners. I'll prepare the draft of my resume and the promotion plan, and see you on Tuesday! I look forward to working together to do something for the stray animals on campus, expressing the core values of freedom and diverse experiences. Remember the picture of the little dog running in a wheelchair from session 5? 'Life always finds a way'—now we can use technology to help them find a better way.

Go for it! Technology changes the world, starting from small things. I'm going to get to work now, let's stay in touch. From health management to gaming field research, to campus public welfare, every collaboration reminds me of what you said in session 1: 'Redefining health issues as interesting projects that require technological solutions'—now we've also defined animal adoption as such a project.
